text: {"observations":"Spectrum is tonal throughout (noisiness 0-3), with energy concentrated at 250-1000 Hz in discrete peaks (about 256, 367, 453, 633 Hz) and many separate onsets, which looks like voices or animal/bird calls rather than weather noise. A steady narrow band at about 3.8-4.0 kHz persists for the whole 10 s, consistent with insects or birds in the background. There is almost no energy above 6 kHz (about -70 to -90 dB), so no broadband hiss as rain would give; this argues against (C). The 0-125 Hz band is weaker than the mid bands and there is no fluctuating noisy low-frequency rumble, which argues against (A). Nothing in the measurements indicates snow (D), which has no distinctive sound anyway. With no audible weather noise and clear ambient tonal sounds, calm (B) is the best inference, though it rests on absence of wind/rain signatures rather than a positive cue.","answer":"B"}
